text:
Eva: Heads-up — FP8 canary running on h100 + l40s. Seeing small but consistent drift on long-context tails, plus sporadic NaN on seq_len > 8k. Posting quick notes + logs.

Alex: thanks. which model/test? can you paste the failing generation example?

Eva: model: rwx-13b-open. test: internal longform eval (8k-12k tokens) + mmlu subset + embedding-regression. Example tokens around 9.3k -> output truncated then NaN in decoder loop.

Mike: ugh. NaNs sound like activation saturation. Did you enable bias rescale/activation-clamp? default fp8 shim uses scale + max_clip=127.

Eva: we ran with ENV: ENABLE_FP8=true, FP8_CLIP=127, FP8_MODE=hybrid. Canary command below:
```
./deploy_canary.sh --model rwx-13b-open --device h100 --quant fp8 --canary_size=30
export ENABLE_FP8=1
export FP8_CLIP=127
```

Jon: curious if this is tiling/KV-cache related. We changed tile_size on l40s to 256 -> might mismatch GEMM alignment with fp8 kernels. Seen soft-drift before when prefix cache reorders.

Eva: stack trace: decoder matmul produced inf at attn_kv_update -> subsequent exp() overflows. Logging attached lines:
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:23Z] ATT: attn_kv_update: max_act=1.2e3 -> scale_update=1e-3 -> quantized overflow
[2026-03-18T14:12:23Z] NAN at decoder_step(9321)
```

Sara: quick eval numbers from canary vs fp16 baseline (mean across 30 runs):
- Perplexity: fp16=12.40, fp8=12.62 (+1.78%)
- MMLU (subset): fp16=73.2, fp8=72.6 (-0.82%)
- Embedding cosine sim (anchor): mean 0.998 -> 0.995 (drop 0.003)
- Throughput: h100 +20% tokens/s, l40s +14%

Mike: 1.8% perp and ~0.8% mmlu drop — borderline acceptable depending on SLOs. But NaNs are showstopper.

Alex: do we see difference between fp8-e4m3 vs e5m2 configs? maybe activation range encoding matters.

Eva: tried e4m3 and hybrid; e4m3 had slightly worse MMLU but fewer NaNs. e5m2 avoided NaNs but larger perp delta. weird.

Jon: tile_size/stride conversation: if GEMM uses different pack for h100 kernels vs l40s kernels we could mis-handle tail tiles. Suggest reproduce with seq_len sweep and dump per-layer max_act.

Eva: agreed. I'll run sweep script and collect layer-wise max_act + scale history. Running now, ETA ~ 2h. Command:
```
python tools/fp8_sweep.py --model rwx-13b-open --devices h100,l40s --seqs "2048,4096,8192,10240,12288" --dump-layer-max
```

InfraBot: deploy-canary job 1769998888 started on h100 (canary id=canary-23). Logs at https://ci.redwood/infer/canary-23

Sara: also add eval on our regression prompt set (few-shot instructions) — some semantic hallucination freq increased ~2% in quick run.

Mike: mitigation ideas:
- enforce per-layer activation clipping before quant
- dynamic scaling with EMA of max_act (long-tail aware)
- fallback routing: if layer_scale > thresh then route request to fp16 variant

Alex: +1 to fallback routing. Add a fast check at kernel entry: if observed_scale > 1e2 -> return fallback.

Jon: I'll prototype a kernel guard that returns a status code instead of in-place NaN. Then runtime can route to fp16 or retry with larger clip. PR idea.

Eva: action items:
- Eva: run seq sweep + dump logs (2h)
- Jon: prototype kernel guard + unit test (1d)
- Mike: try alternate scale/clamp heuristics in local runs (today)
- Sara: run regression suite on current canary and push to dashboard (today)

Alex: thanks team. keep channel updated. If NaNs reappear, we'll pause canary and promote fp16 fallback.

Sara: noted. tagging @platform-oncall for potential canary pause if >2 NaNs in 30 runs :alarm_clock:

InfraBot: canary health: 28/30 runs completed, 3 had NaN events -> marking unstable.

Eva: pausing canary now and rolling back to fp16 for production traffic. Will share sweep artifacts once ready.

Mike: thanks. Good catch, Eva. We'll reconvene after artifacts. :thumbsup:
